description: Phase 9 certified the year-end annualization with the 13th month ACCRUED at year end (regular runs never pay it). Phase 10 certifies a 13th month actually PAID inside a cutoff and the December binding. A 13th month is paid as an approved supplementary earning of type 13th_month; the engine exempts it up to the shared PHP 90,000 pool (remaining pool after any earlier bonus), taxes the excess in that cutoff, and the year-end annualization must then agree with the 24 payslips it summarizes. The December binding annualizes with the freshly calculated final cutoff included, binds the approved adjustment to that run, and the recalculated final payslip must carry it. One organization, all 24 cutoffs of 2026, four monthly employees. Every expected value is hand-derived below from the published rules, never copied from engine output.

sources.thirteenthMonthAndBenefits: NIRC Sec. 32(B)(7)(e) as amended by TRAIN: 13th-month pay and other benefits (including bonuses) share ONE exemption of PHP 90,000 per year; the excess is taxable compensation. PD 851: 13th-month pay is one twelfth of basic salary earned in the calendar year.
sources.contributions: SSS employee 5% of the monthly salary credit (cap 35,000, so at most 1,750 a month); PhilHealth employee 2.5% of monthly basic salary (floor 10,000, cap 100,000 so at most 2,500 a month); Pag-IBIG employee 2% of a fund salary capped at 10,000 (200 a month). With 'split' timing each cutoff carries half.

assumptions: Tax year 2026, 24 semi-monthly cutoffs, each paid on its last day, 'split' statutory timing. No attendance deductions, loans, allowances or leave.

13th month and bonus are approved supplementary earnings that are not part of the SSS or Pag-IBIG base (includeInSssBase and includeInPagIbigBase are false), so contributions are unchanged in the cutoff that pays them.

Cutoffs 1-23 are set to Released in the fixture. Cutoff 24 (periodEnd 2026-12-31) stays in Needs review, is annualized with the run included and bound, and is then recalculated, exactly as the year-end route does. Release approval and the HTTP route are not exercised.

Cutoff withholding applies the semi-monthly table to that cutoff's taxable compensation alone; the engine keeps no year-to-date tax, so any difference to the annual tax is settled only by the year-end adjustment.

paidThirteenthWithinCap.description: PHP 30,000/month; a 30,000 13th month is paid in cutoff 23 (Dec 15). Normal cutoff: gross 15,000; SSS 750, PhilHealth 375, Pag-IBIG 100; taxable 13,775; withholding 15% x (13,775 - 10,417) = 503.70; net 13,271.30. Cutoff 23: gross 45,000; the whole 30,000 is exempt (pool 0 -> 30,000), so taxable stays 13,775 and withholding 503.70; net 45,000 - 1,225 - 503.70 = 43,271.30. Year-end: gross 24 x 15,000 + 30,000 = 390,000, 13th month 30,000 already paid so nothing is accrued; contributions 29,400; non-taxable 59,400; taxable 330,600; tax 15% x 80,600 = 12,090.00; withheld 24 x 503.70 = 12,088.80; collect 1.20. This is identical to the Phase 9 accrual case, so paying the 13th month changes nothing about the annual result. Bound to cutoff 24: net 13,271.30 - 1.20 = 13,270.10 with a year-end tax line of -1.20.

paidThirteenthAboveCap.description: PHP 120,000/month; a 120,000 13th month is paid in cutoff 23. Normal cutoff: gross 60,000; SSS 875 (MSC cap); PhilHealth 2.5% x 100,000 cap = 2,500/month -> 1,250; Pag-IBIG 100; taxable 60,000 - 2,225 = 57,775; withholding 4,270.70 + 25% x (57,775 - 33,333) = 10,381.20; net 47,393.80. Cutoff 23: gross 180,000; only 90,000 is exempt, so 30,000 is taxable: taxable 180,000 - 90,000 - 2,225 = 87,775; withholding 16,770.70 + 30% x (87,775 - 83,333) = 18,103.30; net 180,000 - 2,225 - 18,103.30 = 159,671.70. Year-end: gross 23 x 60,000 + 180,000 = 1,560,000; 13th month 120,000 (entitlement 1,440,000 / 12 equals what was paid); exempt 90,000; contributions 53,400; non-taxable 143,400; taxable 1,416,600; tax 102,500 + 25% x 616,600 = 256,650.00; withheld 23 x 10,381.20 + 18,103.30 = 256,870.90; refund 220.90 (the cutoff table taxed the 30,000 excess at 30% where the annual table taxes it at 25%). Bound to cutoff 24: net 47,393.80 + 220.90 = 47,614.70 with a year-end tax line of +220.90.

partialThirteenthPaid.description: PHP 60,000/month; only 30,000 of the 60,000 entitlement is paid in cutoff 23, so the remaining 30,000 must be accrued at year end. Normal cutoff: gross 30,000; SSS 875; PhilHealth 2.5% x 60,000 = 1,500 -> 750; Pag-IBIG 100; taxable 30,000 - 1,725 = 28,275; withholding 937.50 + 20% x (28,275 - 16,667) = 3,259.10; net 25,015.90. Cutoff 23: gross 60,000; the 30,000 is exempt, so taxable 28,275 and withholding 3,259.10; net 55,015.90. Year-end: entries gross 24 x 30,000 + 30,000 = 750,000; entitlement 720,000 / 12 = 60,000, paid 30,000, accrued 30,000, so gross 780,000; exempt 60,000; contributions 41,400; non-taxable 101,400; taxable 678,600; tax 22,500 + 20% x 278,600 = 78,220.00; withheld 24 x 3,259.10 = 78,218.40; collect 1.60. Bound to cutoff 24: net 25,015.90 - 1.60 = 25,014.30, year-end line -1.60.

bonusThenThirteenthSharePool.description: PHP 60,000/month; a 60,000 bonus in cutoff 12 (Jun 30) and the 60,000 13th month in cutoff 23 share one 90,000 pool. Cutoff 12: gross 90,000; pool before 0, so the whole bonus is exempt; taxable 90,000 - 60,000 - 1,725 = 28,275; withholding 3,259.10; net 90,000 - 1,725 - 3,259.10 = 85,015.90. Cutoff 23: gross 90,000; pool before 60,000, remaining exemption 30,000, so 30,000 of the 13th month is exempt and 30,000 taxable: taxable 90,000 - 30,000 - 1,725 = 58,275; withholding 4,270.70 + 25% x (58,275 - 33,333) = 10,506.20; net 90,000 - 1,725 - 10,506.20 = 77,768.80. Year-end: entries gross 24 x 30,000 + 60,000 + 60,000 = 840,000; entitlement 720,000 / 12 = 60,000, fully paid; pool 60,000 + 60,000 = 120,000, exempt 90,000; contributions 41,400; non-taxable 131,400; taxable 708,600; tax 22,500 + 20% x 308,600 = 84,220.00; withheld 23 x 3,259.10 + 10,506.20 = 85,465.50; refund 1,245.50. Bound to cutoff 24: net 25,015.90 + 1,245.50 = 26,261.40, year-end line +1,245.50.

limitations: Only monthly salaried employees with no attendance, loans, allowances or leave; daily and hourly workers and attendance pay are not run across a year.
The year-end route's HTTP layer, role and MFA gates, settlement after release, and the numbered-2316 reconciliation are not exercised; the library functions the route calls are.
Release approval is bypassed: cutoffs 1-23 are set to Released in the fixture.
13th month and bonus are exempt from the SSS and Pag-IBIG base by fixture choice (includeInSssBase false); how those bases treat a real company's benefit setup is not certified here.
Imported prior-provider history, prior-employer and PERA evidence, minimum wage earners and final-pay (Phase 7) interactions are not covered.
No practitioner has reviewed the expected values; they are derived from the cited rules and need a qualified Philippine payroll/tax review before being relied on for filing.
